indicator.subject: Mathematics
indicator.content_standard: B5.1.1.1 Demonstrate an understanding of quantities and place value for multi-digit numerals up to 1000,000
indicator.objective: Model number quantities up to 1,000,000 using graph sheets and multi-base block

skills.description: Model quantities up to 1,000,000 using multi-base materials (cube = 1,000; rod = 10,000; flat = 100,000; block = 1,000,000).
Model quantities using graph sheets where a square represents a given large value (e.g., 1 cm² = 1,000 units).
Explain the value of a digit in a 6- or 7-digit number.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions: 5 at difficulty 1, 7 at difficulty 2, 5 at difficulty 3, 3 at difficulty 4.
misconceptions: Confusing the values of the multi-base blocks at this scale (e.g., thinking a flat = 10,000 instead of 100,000).
Ignoring zero placeholders when building numbers.
Thinking 1,000,000 is the absolute limit of numbers.

questions.stem: In multi-base materials for large numbers, a flat represents 100,000 and a rod represents 10,000. How many flats and rods are needed to model 320,000?
hints: The first digit tells you the number of 100,000s.
The second digit tells you the number of 10,000s.
questions.explanation: 320,000 has a 3 in the hundred-thousands place (3 flats) and a 2 in the ten-thousands place (2 rods).
questions.misconception: Reversing the number of flats and rods.

questions.stem: If one cube represents 1,000 units, how many cubes are needed to model 7,000?
What is the value of the digit 4 in the number 540,000?
hints: The 4 is in the ten-thousands place.
questions.explanation: The digit 4 is in the ten-thousands place, so its value is 40,000.

questions.stem: On a graph sheet, 1 square represents 10,000 units. How many squares are needed to model 60,000?
In the number 782,000, what does the digit 8 represent?
hints: Count the places from right to left.
questions.explanation: The 8 is in the ten-thousands place, so it represents 8 ten-thousands (80,000).

questions.stem: A learner builds 405,000 using multi-base materials. How many rods are needed if a rod = 10,000?
questions.explanation: The ten-thousands digit is 0, so 0 rods are needed.
questions.misconception: Saying 4 rods because of the 4 in the hundred-thousands place.

questions.stem: A graph sheet uses 1 square to represent 100,000 units. How many squares are needed to model 700,000?
What is the value of the digit 6 in the number 1,600,000?
hints: The 6 is in the hundred-thousands place.
questions.explanation: The digit 6 is in the hundred-thousands place, so its value is 600,000.

questions.stem: If a block represents 1,000,000 and a flat represents 100,000, what is the value of 2 blocks and 5 flats?
On a graph sheet where 1 square = 10,000 units, how many squares represent 150,000?
Explain the difference between the 3 in 3,000,000 and the 3 in 300,000.
hints: Where is the 3 in each number?
questions.explanation: In 3,000,000 the 3 is in the millions place, so it means 3,000,000. In 300,000 the 3 is in the hundred-thousands place, so it means 300,000.

criteria.description: Explains the value of 3 in 3,000,000 is 3,000,000.
Explains the value of 3 in 300,000 is 300,000.

questions.misconception: Thinking the digit 3 has the same value regardless of position.

questions.stem: A pupil models 1,234,000 using blocks, flats, and rods (1 block = 1,000,000; 1 flat = 100,000; 1 rod = 10,000). How many flats are needed?
questions.explanation: The hundred-thousands digit is 2, so 2 flats are needed.
questions.misconception: Saying 3 flats because of the 3 in the ten-thousands place.

questions.stem: A graph sheet uses 1 square for 50,000 units. How many squares are needed to model 475,000?
questions.explanation: 9.5 squares (or 9 full squares and half a square).

questions.stem: A pupil says the value of the digit 5 in 5,230,000 is 50,000. Is the pupil correct? Explain.
hints: Where is the 5? What place value is it?
questions.explanation: The pupil is incorrect. The 5 is in the millions place, so its value is 5,000,000, not 50,000.

criteria.description: Explains the 5 is in the millions place.

questions.stem: Describe how you would model 3,040,000 using blocks, flats, rods, and cubes (block=1,000,000; flat=100,000; rod=10,000; cube=1,000).
hints: Break the number into millions, hundred-thousands, ten-thousands, thousands.
questions.explanation: You need 3 blocks (3,000,000), 0 flats (0), 4 rods (40,000), and 0 cubes (0).
questions.misconception: Forgetting that zero placeholders mean no blocks of that type.

questions.stem: A graph sheet uses 1 square = 20,000 units. How many squares represent 180,000?
What is the value of the digit 9 in the number 9,876,543?
hints: The 9 is in the millions place.
questions.explanation: The digit 9 is in the millions place, so its value is 9,000,000.

questions.stem: Explain how to use a graph sheet to model 1,250,000 if 1 square represents 250,000 units.
A learner models 2,750,000 using 2 blocks, some flats, some rods, and some cubes. How many flats are needed? (block=1,000,000; flat=100,000; rod=10,000; cube=1,000)
questions.explanation: The hundred-thousands digit is 7, so 7 flats are needed.
questions.misconception: Saying 5 flats because of the 5 in the ten-thousands place.
